cases.expected: Num instance representing the first element of the internal list (e.g., DecimalNum.valueOf(100))
cases.description: When the list contains at least one element and the index is 0, getValue should return the element at position 0.

cases.expected: Num instance representing the third element of the internal list (e.g., DecimalNum.valueOf(300))
cases.description: When the index points to a middle element of a non‑empty list, getValue must return the correct Num object.

cases.expected: Num instance representing the last element of the internal list (e.g., DecimalNum.valueOf(500))
cases.description: When the index equals list.size()‑1, getValue should correctly return the last element.
When the provided index is negative, List#get throws IndexOutOfBoundsException; getValue should propagate this exception.
For a list of size 5 (indices 0‑4), an index equal to the size is out of range and should cause IndexOutOfBoundsException.
When the index is larger than the last valid index, getValue must throw IndexOutOfBoundsException.
If the internal values list is empty, any index (including 0) is invalid and should result in IndexOutOfBoundsException.

cases.expected: Num instance representing the sole element (e.g., DecimalNum.valueOf(42))
cases.description: When the list contains exactly one Num element, getValue(0) must return that same Num instance.
If the internal list stores a null at the requested position, getValue should return null without throwing an exception.
If the internal `values` list reference is null, calling `getValue` should throw a NullPointerException when attempting to invoke `values.get(index)`.
When `index` is Integer.MAX_VALUE, it is far beyond the list size and should result in an IndexOutOfBoundsException.
When `index` is Integer.MIN_VALUE (a large negative number), the underlying list access should throw IndexOutOfBoundsException.
